hypotheses.refined_statement: The v2 admissibility rule gap <= 0.1 x dense error is practically unattainable for any two independently stepped O(tol) trajectories: it fails in 54/54 committed rows (18 effective cases x 3 replicas, min ratio 0.1245), in 89-94% of same-code-path admissible pairs and in 88-94% of SciPy Radau pairs. It is attainable only when both arms share a grid-locked step sequence (clipped-vs-clipped 16/18 pass), and the clipped arm is in fact a fixed-step h=span/100 run. The 54/54 nonpass therefore carries no solver information. Scope: n=96 runs; 'both-correct' means reference-admissible (only 6 pairs are within case tolerance, all 6 violate).

The premise holds (max-grid error is ~42x the final-endpoint error) but the attribution is refuted on the campaign corpus: interpolated-point error is only 0.70-2.43x (median 1.08) the accepted-step error, the large ratio being a transient-decay effect. What survives: (i) the interpolant is structurally never tolerance-controlled and on a synthetic stiff Prothero-Robinson problem exceeds tolerance 17-610x (Python replica only); (ii) the dense-arm global error exceeds case tolerance in 12/18 rows (up to 207x on the semilinear family) while every accepted embedded norm is <= 1, i.e. the problem is global error carried by accepted steps, cause not yet attributed.

Order 5 is not preserved under inexact Krylov stage solves: on the pre-specified advection-diffusion problem GMRES with eta=1e-9 keeps 1 clean halving and the production forcing rule 2, versus 4 for direct LU. The predicted mechanism is corrected: eta does loosen (h^-1.1 to h^-1.9) but never reaches the 0.5 clamp (eta_max <= 1e-5); the floor arises because tau = 0.1/||b||_1 is an h-independent absolute stage-residual budget (rhs_wrms-dominated K-form), giving an error floor at 0.1-0.3 rtol, and the 64*eps guard aborts on legal stiff input at tight rtol. The adaptive path stays within tolerance (err/rtol 0.01-0.29). Confounder: direct LU itself shows order 3-4 on stiff Prothero-Robinson, so order loss there is not attributable to inexactness alone. Caveats: single harness, P1PR variant post hoc, FD-JVP arm not run.

Descriptively supported: since v3.6 the tree gained 83 schema families and 4744 prose lines with zero admitted results and zero candidate executions; key scientific bytes exist only in a dirty local worktree; a sealed replay test fails and is run by no workflow; the v3.5 holdout pass rests on one unsafe event inside a one-rank margin. This is a count-based observation with no baseline ratio and no forking-path analysis; it is a productivity/assurance risk, not a falsified result.

Internal BDF/Radau comparators are handicapped (outer-tolerance-independent Newton tolerances, fresh Jacobian+LU per implicit solve, extra estimator LU in RadauIIA3) so no relative performance claim is admissible, which the tree already forbids. The plan's 'J+LU every Newton iteration' is refuted (modified Newton, one LU per solve). Handicap magnitude is unmeasured (code reading only). External SciPy Radau shares rtol/atol with the v2 arm but not step-controller settings; at equal tolerance VigilODE's dense global error is larger in 17/18 rows (median ~2.6x, single-source, accuracy not efficiency).

Supported by static reading only: fair-ab build.rs invokes git 6-7 times with expect/assert, so rodas5p-fair-ab and (via dependency) rodas5p-cli cannot build from a tarball or without git; the failure is a build-script panic at compile time. Additionally any untracked file flips the embedded dirty flag. Neither requirement is documented. No git-less build was actually attempted.
